title: Swap two elements in place
starter:
%b  = buffer 4 dtype=i32 slot=0 data=[1 2 3 4]
# Swap b[0] and b[1]. Leave b[2] and b[3] alone.
%e0 = shrink %b 0 shape=[]
%e1 = shrink %b 1 shape=[]
%x  = load %e0
%y  = load %e1
%s0 = store %e0 %y
%b1 = after %b %s0
hints: The starter writes b[0] but never writes b[1]. You need a second store, and it has to happen after the first one.
A second store into `%b` is invalid (two stores into one version). Store into a view of `%b1`, then sequence it with `after %b1 ...`.
Both values were loaded from the original `%b` before anything was written, so `%x` still holds the old b[0]. Store `%x` into `shrink %b1 1 shape=[]`.
explain: Both loads read version `%b`, so they see the original values. The first store makes `%b1` with b[0] replaced. The second store writes `%x` into a view of `%b1` (call it `%s1`), and `after %b1 %s1` makes the final version. Each version gets exactly one store, so the order is total.
